source: Calvo Figueras & Agerri (2025) Benchmarking Critical Questions Generation
finding: First benchmark for LLMs that write critical questions (CQs) for debate speeches. Reference questions came from Walton scheme templates. Hard task: no model passes 56% useful.
numbers: 220 interventions, 4,976 CQs (22.4 per item). Validation 186/4,136; test 34/806. Labels Useful/Unhelpful/Invalid: 60.91/23.21/15.88% overall; test 42.68/31.02/26.30%. Annotator kappa 0.54.
quote: no LLM generates more than 56% of useful critical questions
limits: Small set. Scores likely underestimated: many generated questions match no reference (not evaluable, about 35% on original test).
agent_relevance: S4 question lists are not solved by a plain LLM; a fixed template list per scheme is the anchor, and free LLM questions need a checker.

source: Calvo Figueras & Agerri (2025) Benchmarking Critical Questions Generation (model table)
finding: Zero-shot generation scores for 11 LLMs. Bigger or closed models lead, but gaps are small. Reasoning-distilled models did not help.
numbers: Mean score: claude-3.5-sonnet 56.65, o4-mini 54.14, gpt-4o 53.70, gemma-2-27b 53.38, Llama-3-70B 52.62, Qwen2.5-VL-72B 51.96, R1-Distill-70B 51.40, gemma-2-9b 50.11, Llama-3-8B 48.16, Qwen-7B 43.51, R1-Distill-8B 41.79. Each Useful question adds 0.33.
limits: Zero-shot, one prompt, test set only (34 items).
agent_relevance: Spread across 11 models is only about 15 points; model choice matters less than the scaffold. Do not rely on model size for S4.

source: Calvo Figueras & Agerri (2025) Benchmarking Critical Questions Generation (diversity and tuning)
finding: o4-mini gave the most diverse questions. Prompt tuning, few-shot and fine-tuning barely moved results.
numbers: n-gram diversity o4-mini 2.76 vs Qwen-7B 0.97. CR-div .332 vs .123. Tuning effects not reported because negligible.
limits: Authors give no tuning detail.
agent_relevance: Prompt wording alone will not fix S4; structure (scheme plus template) is the lever.

source: Calvo Figueras & Agerri (2025) Benchmarking Critical Questions Generation (evaluation method)
finding: Judging generated CQs: reference-based LLM matching agrees with humans; label-only LLM judging does not.
numbers: Cohen kappa with manual reference: claude_reference 0.57, gemma2_reference 0.45, embedding match 0.40 to 0.48. LLM labelling with no references below 0.1. Against manual labels claude_reference 0.28 to 0.41 after adding 1,326 references.
limits: Reference sets must be large (68.6 per item after augmentation) to cover valid questions.
agent_relevance: An LLM cannot grade its own CQs reliably without a reference list; our code should use fixed scheme CQ templates as references.

source: Calvo Figueras & Agerri (2024) Critical Questions Generation: Motivation and Challenges
finding: Two 13B chat models asked zero-shot for CQs mostly produced irrelevant or non-critical questions, but some were valid new ones beyond Walton templates.
numbers: 495 candidate CQs; 308 (62%) relevant. Llama-2-13B query-only 80.74% relevant, with definition 70.7%. Zephyr-13B query-only 67.57%, with definition 29.46%. 207 valid kept (52 match theory CQs, 155 new), 28% of candidates.
limits: Only 21 interventions (60 arguments) analysed; 2 old open models; validity agreement 0.65.
agent_relevance: Adding a CQ definition to the prompt made small models worse (Zephyr 67.6 to 29.5). Keep prompts short.

source: Calvo Figueras & Agerri (2024) Critical Questions Generation: Motivation and Challenges (theory CQs)
finding: Template CQs from Walton et al. (2008) need human editing to fit the content, but annotators agree on filling scheme slots.
numbers: 129 theory-CQs for 51 arguments; slot-annotation agreement 0.88 over 174 variables; 39.44% of questions needed post-editing; 10 discarded. 18 most frequent schemes from US2016 and Moral Maze.
limits: English debate data only.
agent_relevance: Slot-filling a scheme is reliable; question wording needs adaptation. Code can fill slots then let the model reword.

source: Calvo Figueras & Agerri (2024) Critical Questions Generation: Motivation and Challenges (LLM vs theory)
finding: LLM questions overlap theory questions only partly. 16% of LLM CQs ask for definitions of terms, a type missing from the templates.
numbers: 36 unique LLM CQs matched a theory CQ (52 pairs); 242 linked to an argument but matched no theory CQ, 155 of them (64.05%) valid. Validity agreement kappa 0.65.
limits: Unmatched LLM questions elsewhere were not validated.
agent_relevance: Run both: template CQs for coverage, model CQs for gaps such as definitions.

source: Calvo Figueras & Agerri (2024) Critical Questions Generation: Motivation and Challenges (coverage)
finding: LLM candidates touched 50 of 51 annotated arguments, so coverage of arguments is high; the issue is precision.
numbers: 191 unique LLM CQs matched at least one argument across 50 of 51 arguments.
limits: Same small sample.
agent_relevance: Scheme-aware generation should favour precision filters over more generation.

source: Castagna, Sassoon & Parsons (2024) Critical-Questions-of-Thought
finding: Prompting pipeline: sketch premises and conclusion, answer 8 critical questions, gate the answer on a pass threshold (7/8, relaxed to 5/8). Beats standard and CoT on MT-Bench reasoning and math.
numbers: GPT-4o judge, 1-10. Reasoning standard/CoT/CQoT: Claude 3.5 8.6/8.55/8.95; GPT-4o 8.3/8.2/8.45; Gemini 1.5 8.45/8.25/8.9; Llama3.1-70B 8.05/7.5/8.4; Nemotron-51B 6.75/7.7/7.3. Math: Claude 9.25/9.8/9.8; GPT-4o 9.5/8.95/9.6; Gemini 8.75/8.85/9.65; Llama 8.95/9.35/9.55; Nemotron 8.75/8.55/9.15. Text states about +4.6% reasoning, +5.4% math.
limits: 40 questions per model; judge re-prompted until 3 equal scores; MT-Bench may be contaminated; CoT beat CQoT for Nemotron reasoning; temperatures differ.
agent_relevance: Closest published use of CQs inside a gated reasoning loop. Gains are modest (0.1 to 0.6 points) and noisy.

source: Castagna et al. (2024) CQoT ablation
finding: Dropping the CQ step (plan only, steps 1 and 4) gives a score between baseline and full CQoT, so CQs add value beyond the plan.
numbers: Llama reasoning 8.05 to 8.3 (plan only) to 8.4 (full); math 8.95 to 9.25 to 9.55. Nemotron reasoning 6.75 to 6.85 to 7.3; math 8.75 to 9.0 to 9.15.
limits: Two models only; no variance reported; summary percentages inconsistent with Table 3.
agent_relevance: Supports keeping S4 as a separate step, not folding it into the plan. Effect about half from plan, half from CQs.

source: Castagna et al. (2024) CQoT cost and limits
finding: Pipeline can take seconds to minutes per answer; authors suspect a model-size threshold near 70B but did not test it.
numbers: Five models: Claude 3.5, GPT-4o, Gemini 1.5-pro, Llama 3.1-70B, Nemotron-51B. Threshold 7/8 CQs passed then 5/8.
limits: Generic CQs, not scheme-specific; Toulmin-based, not Walton schemes.
agent_relevance: Our S4 uses scheme-specific CQs run by code, which this paper did not test; an open slot.

source: Favero et al. (2025) ELLIS Alicante at CQs-Gen 2025 (winner)
finding: Winning system: a small Questioner LLM writes 8 candidate CQs, a Judge LLM picks the best 3. Llama 3.1 8B plus Gemma 2 9B.
numbers: Final automatic score on test: sub1 36.3%, sub2 44.1%, sub3 (GPT-4o both roles) 50.0% useful, with 28 to 36% not evaluable. After manual annotation the best submission scored 67.6, rank 1.
limits: Dataset small; automatic metric undercounts; own test split 79 items.
agent_relevance: Generate-many-then-select is a working pattern for S4 (generation vs evaluation split).

source: Favero et al. (2025) ELLIS (scheme ablation)
finding: Putting scheme names, definitions and question templates in the prompt helps, but only when mixed with unconstrained prompts.
numbers: Llama 3.1 8B, 6 questions, Gemma 2 judge: useful after judge: Without schemes about 57.7, With one-prompt about 56.5, scheme per prompt 51.6, Both 62.4. 81% of judge-selected questions came from scheme prompts.
limits: Table text partly garbled in PDF extraction; read values as approximate except Both 62.4. Strict schemes lowered diversity.
agent_relevance: Use schemes for half the candidates, free generation for the rest.

source: Favero et al. (2025) ELLIS (judge value)
finding: The LLM judge adds only a little over random choice; most of the gap to the oracle is not closed.
numbers: Judge +3.4 points useful over random (p<0.05, McNemar). Oracle +34.2 points (93.5% useful). Gemma 2 judge 55.9%; 3 runs.
limits: Oracle is an upper bound that uses labels.
agent_relevance: Selecting questions is the weak link; a code-run template check may beat an LLM judge.

source: Favero et al. (2025) ELLIS (candidate count, fine-tuning)
finding: 4+4 candidates was best; fine-tuning and BERT data augmentation gave limited gains on the small set.
numbers: Useful %: 6 candidates 59.3, 8 candidates 57.2 or 57.3 (3 runs, Llama 3.1 + Gemma 2); differences within noise.
limits: Small dataset.
agent_relevance: Little to gain from more candidates beyond a handful.

source: Zhou, Saadat-Yazdi & Kokciyan (2025) DayDreamer at CQs-Gen 2025
finding: Three-stage chat pipeline: instantiate Walton scheme templates from the text, generate CQs from templates, rank top 3. GPT-4o-mini and Llama-3.1-8B.
numbers: Test: 4th of 13 teams, 60 Helpful, 25 Unhelpful, 17 Invalid. Validation useful%: direct prompting 56.81, conversational 62.90, +sorted schemes 65.41, +ranking 68.28, minus ER schemes 72.22 (unhelpful 12.01 to 8.78).
limits: Ablation on validation only; one manual run; two GPT runs differed (unstable).
agent_relevance: Scheme-slot completion plus ranking beats direct prompting by about 15 points useful on validation.

source: Zhou et al. (2025) DayDreamer (missing templates)
finding: Four ER-prefixed schemes had no definitions in Walton et al. Filling them with similar schemes confused models; dropping templates helped.
numbers: Removing ER templates: useful 68.28 to 72.22, unhelpful 12.01 to 8.78. About 75% of validation CQs were LLM-made, so overfit risk.
limits: Some schemes lack CQ templates in the book.
agent_relevance: Our scheme library should only include schemes with a vetted CQ list.

source: Hong et al. (2024) ArgMed-Agents
finding: LLM agent loop: Generator proposes, Verifier asks scheme critical questions, Reasoner solves an argumentation framework. Beats direct and CoT on medical QA.
numbers: MedQA/PubMedQA accuracy: GPT-3.5 direct 52.7/68.4, CoT 48.0/71.5, ArgMed 62.1/78.3. GPT-4 direct 67.8/72.9, CoT 71.4/77.2, ArgMed 83.3/81.6. 300 items each.
limits: No ablation, no variance, 300 items, explainability metric uses an unvalidated evaluator.
agent_relevance: Gain over CoT of +11.9 on GPT-4 MedQA is large but unablated; cannot tell if CQs or the solver matter.

source: Hong et al. (2024) ArgMed-Agents (design)
finding: Uses domain schemes (decision making, side effects, danger appeal); generator outputs are treated as assumptions, not facts. Dialogue limit 8, temperature 0.
numbers: Failures analysed: 63% of no-acceptable-decision cases showed identifiable reasoning errors. Explainability evaluator score GPT-4 0.91 vs CoT 0.73.
limits: Authors call this preliminary; few-shot despite zero-shot claim.
agent_relevance: The design (CQs as rejections that return to the generator) maps to an S4 reject-and-retry edge.

source: Ruiz-Dolz et al. (2024) NLAS-multi
finding: GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 can write textbook instances of 20 Walton schemes; humans accept most. Classifiers then label them almost perfectly.
numbers: 3,810 arguments (1,893 EN, 1,917 ES). Valid after GPT-3.5: EN 74.8%, ES 89.7%. GPT-4 fixed 78.8% (EN) and 60% (ES) of the rejects. Kappa EN 0.65, ES 0.22. RoBERTa macro-F1 99.3 EN random split, 99.6 topic-wise.
limits: Templated, complete arguments; no enthymemes; near-perfect F1 reflects template regularity, not real text.
agent_relevance: Scheme recognition on clean text is easy; do not infer it holds on messy input.

source: Ruiz-Dolz & Lawrence (2025) Misinformation via Critical Question Answering
finding: Two-step system: classify scheme, then answer its CQs yes/no; a no flags misinformation. Fine-tuned RoBERTa beats zero-shot GPT-4 at answering CQs.
numbers: CQA macro-F1: RoBERTa 70.7 (73.94 with context), GPT-4 63.5 (62.5 with context), Mixtral-8x7B 28.7 (34.6). Generative models said yes to 53.3% of negative CQs. NLAS-CQ: 3,566 valid (89.1% of 4,000), 4,687 CQ answers over 10 schemes; CQ kappa 0.42.
limits: Context supplied by hand; only 10 schemes have CQ labels; CQ subjectivity high.
agent_relevance: GPT-4 is yes-biased on CQs: it accepts weak arguments. Our code needs a skeptical prior or a forced counter-case.

source: Ruiz-Dolz & Lawrence (2025) (scheme classification on real debate)
finding: Scheme classification collapses on real dialogue arguments with missing premises, unless trained on dialogue and with schemes grouped into families.
numbers: NLAS-CQ macro-F1: random 4.6, SVM 83.0, RoBERTa 99.2. On QT30 debate: plain RoBERTa 1.0, with scheme families 31.7, dialogue data 2.4, both 44.8 (F1).
limits: 287 QT30 schemes, 35% test.
agent_relevance: Scheme selection from raw text is the hard part (99 down to 45). Our code should choose the scheme from a short list with a type tag, not infer it.

source: Pan et al. (2024) Are LLMs Good Zero-Shot Fallacy Classifiers?
finding: Zero-shot LLMs catch fallacies (the failure side of schemes) well on some sets and badly on others. Multi-round prompting helps small models most.
numbers: GPT-4 best zero-shot Macro-F1 vs T5-3B full-shot: Argotario 79.87/72.38, Logic 50.54/64.95, Reddit 81.11/83.20, ElecDeb 41.25/62.37, Propaganda 35.37/43.33, Mafalda 52.86/35.60, Covid-19 25.18/14.59. Multi-round improved 83.7% of runs: +1.6 GPT-4, +7.5 Llama3-8B.
limits: Single-label only; GPT-4 over-predicted No Fallacy on Covid-19.
agent_relevance: Multi-round (one check per round) beats one big prompt; supports asking CQs one at a time.

source: Pan et al. (2024) fallacies (prompt design)
finding: Zero-shot CoT was the most robust prompt; listing premises and conclusion first was worst; formal definitions added little; few-shot helped only GPT-4.
numbers: Premises-and-conclusion prompt: 12.46% failure rate (worst). Zero-shot CoT second best, lowest failure rate among top schemes.
limits: Seven models; label-space and truncation effects.
agent_relevance: Extracting premises first does not by itself help; the question has to be the test.

source: Sarkadi et al. (2026) DeceptionAnalyser
finding: Tool with ten deception schemes, each with CQs; an LLM fills premises with verbatim quotes and answers CQs. Consistency was checked across models and runs.
numbers: Fox and Crow fable: 11 models x 10 runs, all 100 assessments green, within-model stability 1.00, cross-model agreement 1.00. Harder Operation Mincemeat narrative: majority green but two models (gpt-5.4, gpt-oss-20b) abstain more on the unstated major premise. All 600 premise assessments gave a verbatim excerpt.
limits: Reliability study, not accuracy; no ground-truth labels; deep CQ recursion becomes circular.
agent_relevance: Scheme-slot extraction with a quoted source is stable on clear cases; disagreement between models marks the weak inference.

source: Sarkadi et al. (2026) DeceptionAnalyser (failure modes)
finding: Named failures: source-ungrounded inference (F1), CQs with no supporting passage (F2), role inversion in a CQ (F3). Analyst feedback is appended to the element's prompt on rerun.
numbers: Examples in Section 5; counts not given.
limits: Illustrative cases.
agent_relevance: Add a role-consistency check and a quote-or-abstain rule to S4.

source: Henselmans et al. (2026) Measuring AI Accountability Through Argumentation Analysis
finding: Models were asked to defend their own moral verdicts against scheme CQs. Defences fail mostly on grounds and sufficiency.
numbers: 200 MoralChoice dilemmas, 9 models, 6,778 scored cells. Overall failure 18.2%. Claude Sonnet 4.6 54.8% and Llama 3.3 50.6% account for 68% of failures; GPT-5.4 1.0%, DeepSeek 4.3%. Judge agreement 89.6%.
limits: Self-judging (Claude is judge and subject); summary-based traces; 2 judges.
agent_relevance: Models can state a verdict but often cannot answer scheme CQs about it; S4 can expose this.

source: Henselmans et al. (2026) (scheme use)
finding: Models collapse to one scheme (value-based practical reasoning) and switch scheme between reasoning and justification.
numbers: Value-based practical reasoning about 72% of reasoning and 67% of justification labels; argument from consequences 8% to 16% (chi2 55.9). Scheme agreement per model 58% to 80%. Reasoning traces scored higher than post-hoc justifications on all Govier dimensions except local relevance. Commitment stability correlates with grounds (rho 0.27), sufficiency (0.49).
limits: Panel regimes not comparable.
agent_relevance: Scheme choice is unstable; fix the scheme by type in code rather than letting the model drift. Post-hoc rationalisation is weaker than the real reasoning.

source: Disinformation detection with argumentation and LLMs (CMNA 2024, UPV)
finding: Pipeline: classify scheme (19 schemes + no-scheme), generate CQs tailored to content, search Google/Wikipedia/Bing per CQ, then Llama 3 70B gives a truthfulness score.
numbers: NLAS-multi 2,188 EN arguments, 80/20 split. Two-layer classifier (group then scheme) reached 85 to 87% on accuracy, precision, recall, F1; non-scheme precision rose 20.19% to 72.22%. 80 adults rated 20 outputs; 83.8% satisfied.
limits: Rated only by satisfaction, not accuracy of verdicts; synthetic scheme data.
agent_relevance: Retrieval per CQ is an existing way to answer questions with evidence. A grouped two-step scheme choice cut false no-scheme labels.

source: Betz, Voigt & Richardson (2020) Critical Thinking for Language Models
finding: Pre-training GPT-2 on synthetic deductively valid argument schemes improves zero-shot NLU; abstract only was read.
numbers: Up to 15 percentage points on GLUE diagnostics.
limits: Deductive schemes, not defeasible Walton schemes; baseline and sizes not read.
agent_relevance: Early sign that scheme-form training transfers; not relevant to a no-training scaffold.

source: Jo, Bang, Reed & Hovy (2021) Classifying Argumentative Relations Using Logical Mechanisms and Argumentation Schemes
finding: Four theory-based mechanisms (factual consistency, sentiment, causal, normative) classify support/attack/neutral without labels and help supervised models.
numbers: Abstract only: beats unsupervised baselines; no figures read.
limits: Only abstract opened.
agent_relevance: Rule-like checks can sit beside a model.

source: Walton, Reed & Macagno (2008) Argumentation Schemes
finding: Catalogue of about 60 presumptive schemes each with critical questions; the source of nearly all CQ templates used in the LLM work above.
numbers: Not opened this session.
limits: Book not read; claim from memory and from papers above that cite Walton et al. templates.
agent_relevance: Template source for our S4 table.
